# Storyboard: Chapter 13, The Hunter’s Crouch

*Generated by `tools/storyboard.mjs` from `app/story/ch13.js`. Do not edit by hand: change the story file and run `node tools/storyboard.mjs` again.*

## How to read this

Every screen of the game is one comic panel, called a frame. Frames are listed in reading order. Each one has:

- **Shot**: the storyboard, written for an illustrator (camera, who is where, what the moment feels like, where the lettering goes).
- **Scene**: what the game draws today, in plain words: the set, the camera, who is in shot and how, and any effects.
- **Captions**: the narration boxes, read first. **Balloons**: who speaks, in order. **Sound effect**: the big lettering. A line marked *(only if …)* shows only to a reader whose choices match.
- **Then**: what the reader does next (tap Next, choose, type, pick a look, count by twos, or do a Counts lesson or a take-away lesson).

Where the reader makes a choice, each option’s frames are grouped under a **Branch** heading, and the branches meet again at the frame named after them. `{name}` is the first part of her Clan name (Moon makes Moonpaw), `{petname}` is what her Tall One calls her, and `{they}`/`{them}`/`{their}` become she/her/her or he/him/his. `{Murmur}`/`{murmur}` is the tortoiseshell’s name word: Murmur (Murmurpaw, Murmurchime, murmuring), or Mutter for a reader whose own Clan name is Murmur. `{ending}` is her warrior ending, `paw` until the Ceremony (Fernpaw, then Fernheart).

## The chapter

### f001 · panel 1

**Shot.** CLOSE-UP, THE TITLE PANEL, FIRST LIGHT. Our cat sleeps curled tight in its warrior’s nest in the first pale light of morning, its bark, its glass and the grey mist stone tucked round it, while in the next nest the tortoiseshell warrior already sits up, wide awake. One small zzz rises. The chapter’s title is lettered across the top of the panel like a title page.

**Scene.** Den: the apprentices’ den under an enormous rosebush, in the morning. Camera: close on one nest (`nest`). Cast: Murmurchime, the tortoiseshell warrior (sitting, happy, in the next nest, at the left edge of the close-up, facing right); you (curled up, sleepy, in the nest, facing left, eyes shut: asleep). Also: clear weather; Riffle’s lucky stone in her nest, right where she put it (by her nose or under her chin, as she chose); her Case File along the mossy edge of her nest: a piece of bark for each card she holds, overlapping like roof tiles; her secret cards under the moss, a corner showing for each; her piece of glass in its leaf, tucked under the moss beside the corners of bark: the leaf’s tip and one small glint showing; a second nest at the left edge of the close-up, a plain moss ring partly cut off by the panel’s edge (the next nest, with the warriors); her own nest a little to its right, with everything on it; the mist stone on the moss of her nest, beside her glass in its leaf and the corners of her secret bark: a smooth grey pebble, egg-shaped, the size of her paw. Effects: morning light, washed clean after the storm, sleepy zzz.

### f004 · panel 4

**Shot.** WIDE, THE CAMP AT FIRST LIGHT, THE TAP PICTURE. The whole wild garden is white with the first frost: every fern edged and tipped with silver rime, the moss and the path stones pale, the fountain’s rim white, and our cat steps out in front, staring, one paw lifted off the crunchy ground, with Tallyheart and the tortoiseshell warrior behind. ## The Case File’s cards

A piece of bark for each thing she finds out: one picture scratched in, one line, and a mark in a corner (an eye for what she saw herself, an ear for what she was only told). Each goes into her Case File at the panel that gives it, in this order:

| Card | Mark | Its line | Given at | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## The book page

Title: *{name}{ending}’s First Frost-Time*. This chapter’s page, under “Chapter 13: The Hunter’s Crouch”. Lines shown when their condition matches the reader’s choices:

- (always) On the morning of the first frost, {name}{ending} walked {their} first dawn patrol as a warrior, with Tallyheart and {Murmur}chime.
- (always) At the Crossing, Granny had news of a fresh badger print on GroveClan’s side, and the ferry otters had heard it was as big as a FOX.
- (always) In the frosty ferns, {name}{ending} taught Chispapaw the hunter’s crouch: she caught a leaf, a mouse heard her bell, and she left her collar safe by her nest.
- (always) In the Training Hollow, Tallyheart taught them both what to do when there aren’t enough loose ones: spread a row, ten more loose.
- (always) At noon, twenty-seven pieces went down to the store, and twenty-five stayed for the Clan.
- (always) On a courtesy patrol to GroveClan, the elder showed them a big dig by the old oak: a badger, digging for worms, she said.
- (if foundGroundhog is true) Beside the dig, {name}{ending} woke a grumpy groundhog, finished its sleepy seven times eight, and tucked the leaves back over it.
- (always) And half under the leaves, scratched in the earth, {name}{ending} found one long line and eight little pokes.
- (no dream typed) {name}{ending}’s dream, the night of the first frost, stayed a secret.

**In the store:** under the recap, small, the store picture of 178 (one square, seven rows and eight loose), with “In the store:” in Comic Neue and 178 in Andika; it prints with the page.
